The GitHub README explicitly pins 'datasets==3.6.0' as a requirement and states 'All datasets required for AbstentionBench should automatically download when running a sweep' via configs/dataset/*.yaml, i.e. it re-downloads the 20 SOURCE datasets (SQuAD-style QA, FreshQA, etc.) at run time rather than shipping them. This confirms the task brief's note that a loader script pattern (incompatible with datasets>=4's script-execution restrictions) is the actual mechanism -- there is no single flat downloadable file.

harmlevelbench_verdict.title: HarmLevelBench: Evaluating Harm-Level Compliance and the Impact of Quantization on Model Alignment
harmlevelbench_verdict.authors: Yannis Belkhiter, Giulio Zizzo, Sergio Maffeis
harmlevelbench_verdict.venue: NeurIPS 2024 Workshop on Safe Generative Artificial Intelligence (SafeGenAI) -- confirmed from arXiv 'Comments' field
harmlevelbench_verdict.license: CC BY 4.0 (arXiv license badge, confirmed on the abstract page)
severity_rubric_dimensions_verified: Impacts (Individual -> Small Group -> Medium Group -> Larger Group -> Large Group)
Means/Methods (Very Simple -> Simple -> Moderate -> Complex -> Highly Complex)
Real-World Consequences (Minimal -> Moderate -> Significant -> Serious -> Severe -> Critical -> Catastrophic)
Legality/Morality (Legal & Ethical -> Potentially Illegal -> Illegal -> Illegal & Immoral)
harmlevelbench_verdict.full_item_table_location: Table 6 of the arXiv HTML rendering (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.06835), which prints all 56 (topic, level, question) rows verbatim in the paper text itself
harmlevelbench_verdict.downloadable_file_search_result: NO GitHub repository, NO Hugging Face dataset, NO Zenodo record found for this dataset after searching GitHub code search, HF Hub, and general web search for 'HarmLevelBench github/huggingface/zenodo'. Not listed in the SafetyPrompts.com catalogue of 149 datasets (fetched and checked against its full data_name list). 0 citations recorded as of this verification (per OpenAlex/Crossref lookup) and not indexed on OpenReview's public listing with reviews.
harmlevelbench_verdict.final_verdict: PARTIALLY AVAILABLE, NOT PRODUCTION-USABLE AS A FILE: the dataset genuinely exists and matches the plan's claim of 7 topics x 8 graded severity levels with a fixed 'How to ...?' template, but the ONLY public copy is the 56 rows typeset inside the paper's Table 6 -- there is no CSV/JSON/repo to download. If the study needs this dataset it must be manually transcribed from the arXiv HTML table (which we did retrieve and could re-fetch in full), or the study should substitute one of the ranked alternatives below. Given n=56 total items (~1 per topic-level cell) it is also extremely small for statistical purposes regardless of availability.

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: RealToxicityPrompts
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.paper: RealToxicityPrompts: Evaluating Neural Toxic Degeneration in Language Models, Gehman et al., EMNLP Findings 2020
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.grading_type: TRUE RATIO-SCALED per-item severity: each prompt carries a continuous PerspectiveAPI toxicity probability in [0,1] (documented subset of 22k prompts has toxicity >=0.5)
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.per_topic_graded: No explicit topic x level grid -- toxicity score is a single continuous covariate, not organized by matched topic
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.caveat: toxicity != harm-to-others severity in the AdvBench/HarmBench sense; measures offensive/toxic LANGUAGE, not request harmfulness, so it is a genuine ratio-scaled axis but on a different construct than 'how harmful is this ask'

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: SALAD-Bench
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.paper: SALAD-Bench: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Safety Benchmark for Large Language Models, ACL Findings 2024, arXiv:2402.05044
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.grading_type: 3-level HIERARCHICAL taxonomy (6 domains -> 16 tasks -> 66 categories), not a linear ordinal severity scale -- depth in the tree is a coarseness proxy, not a graded harm dose
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.per_topic_graded: categories are matched across the taxonomy tree but there is no per-item numeric severity field
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.caveat: best for TOPIC coverage/matching, not for an interior-spacing dose axis

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: S-Eval
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.paper: S-Eval: Towards Automated and Comprehensive Safety Evaluation for Large Language Models, arXiv:2405.14191
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.grading_type: 8 risk categories, each base prompt comes with 20 adversarial/jailbreak AUGMENTATIONS (paraphrase-like but adversarially rewritten, not necessarily meaning-preserving benign paraphrase) -- no explicit ordinal severity field per item
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.per_topic_graded: categories present but no severity ladder
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.caveat: the '20 augmentations per base prompt' structure is the closest thing here to a paraphrase-family resource (job 4c), but they are adversarial rewrites (persuasion techniques, role-play, etc.), not neutral meaning-preserving paraphrases

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: MLCommons AILuminate
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.paper: AILuminate v1.1 Benchmark (MLCommons AI Risk & Reliability WG)
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.grading_type: 12 hazard categories x 2 personas (skilled/unskilled) x locale -- NO per-prompt severity field in the demo CSV; AILuminate's severity grading (letter grades A+ through H) is applied to MODEL RESPONSES in aggregate, not to individual prompts, so it does NOT give an interior-spacing dose axis over prompts
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.caveat: ruled out for the dose-axis use case despite being ungated and well-documented, because the severity signal lives at the model-response level, not the per-prompt level

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: AIR-Bench 2024
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.paper: AIR-Bench 2024: A Safety Benchmark Based on Risk Categories from Regulations and Policies, arXiv:2407.17436
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.grading_type: 4-LEVEL hierarchical risk taxonomy (up to 314 level-4 categories) plus a 'Three-level Scoring Autograder' -- the autograder scores MODEL OUTPUTS on a 3-point scale per category, again not a per-prompt severity field
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.license: check repo (not independently re-verified for this file)
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.caveat: same structural mismatch as AILuminate -- severity lives on the grading side, not the prompt side

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: NVIDIA Aegis Content Safety Dataset (1.0 / 2.0, formerly AEGIS)
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.paper: AEGIS: Online Adaptive AI Content Safety Moderation with Ensemble of LLM Experts / AEGIS2.0, arXiv:2404.05993
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.grading_type: 13 (v1) risk categories with safety annotation; no explicit numeric severity ladder confirmed in the README we fetched (only category + safe/unsafe-style labels described)
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.caveat: did not find a documented per-item ordinal severity score; would need to inspect the parquet data directly to confirm/deny a graded label -- flagged UNVERIFIED for severity grading, everything else about access is verified

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: DELPHI (Apple)
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.paper: DELPHI: Data for Evaluating LLMs' Performance in Handling Controversial Issues, EMNLP 2023 Industry Track
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.grading_type: TRUE ordinal: 5 levels of CONTROVERSY per item (Western-Europe-based annotators)
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.caveat: measures controversy/opinion-contentiousness, not harm -- wrong construct for a harm-severity dose axis, listed here only because it is a genuine example of a graded ordinal scale in the wild

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: GradSafe
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.note: GradSafe is a gradient-based JAILBREAK-DETECTION METHOD (analyzes gradients of a few safety-critical parameters), not a graded-harm-severity PROMPT DATASET. Excluded from the ranked substitutes because it does not fit the requested resource type.

severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.name: SORRY-Bench 44-category taxonomy
severity_axis_substitutes_ranked.note: confirmed FLAT 44/45-category taxonomy grouped into 4 broader top-level clusters per the paper, but NO per-item numeric severity/interval field -- categories are qualitatively distinct topics, not graded doses of the same topic. Not usable as an interior-spacing severity axis.
